units.text: Motivation: revisit GraphRAG shortcomings from relation extraction errors
GraphRAG systems that rely on pre-extracted relations are vulnerable to error propagation when the extraction step produces incomplete or incorrect edges, degrading downstream retrieval quality.
This work revisits that dependency by adopting a graph-structured retrieval formulation that does not require a separate relation extraction stage, thereby eliminating the error source at its origin.
LinearRAG overview: Tri‑Graph concept and two‑stage retrieval philosophy
The LinearRAG system structures retrieval around a Tri‑Graph, a graph whose three node types—entities, sentences, and passages—are linked by sparse adjacency matrices.

Retrieval proceeds in two stages: the first stage activates entity nodes to perform local semantic bridging, and the second stage propagates importance across the graph (via personalized PageRank) to select passages for global relevance.
